q: In the data-quality-txn project, what do we know about q-dq-late-cause?
a: It asks why cards.txn_daily partitions land after 10:00 on D+1. The 2025-Q1 census found 4.1 percent late, skewed to Mondays and month-starts, and the late share fell to 1.6 percent after the upstream batch moved to 04:30 in October 2025.

q: In the data-quality-txn project, what came of exp-302, the duplicate audit?
a: About 0.31 percent of 2025-Q1 rows were duplicates, concentrated in partitions reloaded after retries. That led to fnd-dup-retries and to dec-dq-dedupe-first-arrival, which keeps the first arrival in the consumer view.

q: In the data-quality-txn project, what does dq-late-logit-v2 use as inputs?
a: Weekday, the month-start flag, the prior day's row count, and a retry flag. The retry flag is new in v2, and the model is evaluated on dq-oot-2025q4.

q: In the data-quality-txn project, what is the current late-partition alert rule?
a: A 06:30 pre-alert when dq-late-logit-v2 gives probability above 0.6, plus the 11:00 not-landed page as the backstop (dec-dq-late-alert-rule-v2). It replaced the time-only v1 rule from July 2025.

q: In the data-quality-txn project, what AUC did the late-partition model v2 reach on dq-oot-2025q4, and what did v1 reach on the same holdout?
a: 0.79 for dq-late-logit-v2 on dq-oot-2025q4 (n=276 checkpoints), against 0.72 for v1 on the same holdout (exp-306).

q: In the data-quality-txn project, why did we switch the volume z-score baseline to the same weekday?
a: The all-weekday baseline raised 41 alarms in 2025-H1, 6.8 per month, mostly on Mondays and weekends. The same-weekday baseline raised 7, or 1.2 per month (exp-304), so dec-dq-same-weekday-baseline adopted it.
